page.title: Folkhold: a Minecraft world that lives on its own
site.name: Folkhold
site.tagline: A single-player Minecraft world that changes without the player.
site.description: NPC factions trade, defend their villages and hold territory. Caravans travel between the villages. The reputation of the player decides how each village receives them.
nav.label: Sections
features.title: A world that lives on its own
features.text: A simulation runs the factions, the stocks and the caravans, also in the chunks that are not loaded. You are one actor among others: the world changes when you are away.
feature.factions.title: Factions and territories
feature.factions.text: Each new world gets 5 to 7 factions. Each faction comes from a culture with its colors, its banner, its names and the style of its buildings. One or two factions are your allies, one is neutral and the others are hostile. Each village claims the territory around it.
feature.villages.title: Fortified villages
feature.villages.text: A faction village is a walled compound with towers, gates and a village heart. Guards patrol, archers hold the towers and a captain leads the garrison. Builders add homes and repair the walls, and the village grows from a hamlet to a city. Kill the captain and destroy the heart: the village becomes ruins.
feature.caravans.title: Caravans and trade
feature.caravans.text: Each village makes and uses goods with the jobs of its inhabitants, and its prices follow its stock. Trade between two villages sends a caravan on the road, by land or by boat: a merchant, mules with chests and guards. Buy from it on the road, escort it, or raid it and lose reputation.
feature.quests.title: Reputation and quests
feature.quests.text: Each faction remembers what you do, from sworn enemy to ally. The quest board of a village gives quests from the state of the world: bring the goods that the village needs, or escort a caravan through the ambushes to its destination. The rewards are emeralds and reputation.
features.also.title: Also in Folkhold
features.also.economy: Villages that grow. The beds of the homes give the places of the inhabitants, and the builders build new homes on the free plots.
features.also.rails: Trains. Link minecarts with a chain and pull them with a furnace locomotive.
features.also.maps: Journal and maps. The journal lists the villages and the factions that you found, with a map of the territories.
features.also.languages: Two languages. All the text of the game is in English and in French.

download.title: Download
download.modpack.title: Modpack (client)
download.modpack.text: The modpack is the simple way to play. It contains the Folkhold mods and a selection of mods for performance, nature, terrain, maps and inventory comfort.
download.modpack.step1: Download the file of the modpack.
download.modpack.step2: Import the file in a launcher that reads Modrinth packs, for example Prism Launcher or the Modrinth App.
download.modpack.step3: Start the game and create a new world.
download.mods.title: Mods
download.mods.text: To use the mods without the modpack, put folkhold_core, folkhold_blocks and folkhold_world in the mods folder of a Minecraft {minecraft} instance. The instance needs NeoForge {neoforge} or later and GeckoLib {geckolib} or later.
download.other.title: Other files
download.more: The README gives more information about the installation.
download.server.title: Server
download.server.text: The server and each player must use the same version of Folkhold.
download.server.step1: Install a NeoForge {neoforge} server for Minecraft {minecraft} with the NeoForge installer (option “Install server”).
download.server.step2: Put the jars of the release and their dependencies (see Mods) in the mods folder of the server. Each player puts the same mods in the client.
download.server.docker: Another way: with Docker, the image itzg/minecraft-server can install the modpack on the server: set TYPE=MODRINTH and give the path of the .mrpack file in MODRINTH_MODPACK. The players then use the modpack.
